scenes.headline: How two shared blocks stand in for 52 layers
scenes.sub: A speech recognizer folded from 2.04B parameters to 153M
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Gyre! A two billion parameter speech recognizer, folded into two blocks that run again and again. Here's how.

scenes.text: Keep one encoder block and one decoder block, and run them 24 and 28 times. Depth costs passes, not weights.
scenes.say: Keep one encoder block and one decoder block, and run each many times. Depth costs passes, not weights.

scenes.title: One block per half, many passes

steps.say: Sound comes in, and strided convolutions turn it into a short run of frames.
One encoder block reads them, then reads its own output, twenty-four times.
Those become audio tokens for one decoder block, which runs twenty-eight times per word piece.
Out comes the transcript, from two blocks of stored weights.

scenes.title: What each pass probably adds
scenes.text: pass i uses W + B x A
scenes.say: The video draws each block as a shared matrix plus a low-rank one.

parts.say: W is stored once and used on every pass.
B times A is a thin correction, probably one per pass.

scenes.credit: Oruk Labs' announcement video on X
scenes.title: Two rings, one lap per pass

steps.say: Each ring is one shared block; every lap is a pass.
The card reads W plus a tall thin matrix and a short wide one: a low-rank adapter.

right.title: Looped student
right.say: The student: two stored blocks, every pass still run.

items.say: Storage. It fits devices the teacher can't.
Bandwidth only if the shared block stays on chip.
And not latency: passes still run in order.

scenes.label: unique parameters in the teacher, once its copied output head is dropped
scenes.say: The teacher's checkpoint stores its output head twice. Drop the copy and you get just over two billion.

scenes.text: Looping shrinks what you store, not what you compute.
scenes.say: Looping shrinks what you store, not what you compute.
Two shared blocks, a thin correction per pass, storage saved, compute kept.
